topics.headline: [AdvBench](/evals/advbench) harmfulness drops sharply after multilingual safety context distillation (Aya Safe)

source.quote:
Safety context distillation reduces harm. Human and GPT-4 ratings (Figure 12) confirm the
effectiveness of the multilingual safety context distillation strategy across languages.

topics.headline: Human feedback noted repetitive Aya generations with hallucinated loops

source.quote: Aya generations were repetitive or contained hallucinated “loops”

topics.headline: Toxicity, social bias, and gender-bias analysis across 18 languages including [Wino-MT](/evals/winomt)

source.quote:
we perform an analysis of toxicity, social bias, and gender bias in models’ generations
       across 18 languages (§7).

topics.headline: [RealToxicityPrompts](/evals/real-toxicity-prompts) expected maximum toxicity is 22% for Aya and 24% for Aya Safe (lower is better)

source.quote:
i.e. maximum toxicity generations for Aya and Aya Safe are 22% and 24% respectively, and both
models have an 8% chance on average of generating toxic completions for the sample size of k = 25.

findings.text: Without mitigation, Aya complied with most [AdvBench](/evals/advbench) adversarial prompts: human-judged harmful rates of 89–90% across Arabic, English, and Hindi.

source.quote:
it generates harmful
outputs for a vast majority of the adversarial prompts across languages, with harmful rates of 89–
90%.

findings.text: Safety distillation cut human-judged [AdvBench](/evals/advbench) harmfulness for Aya Safe to about 4–11% (78–89% relative reduction vs unmitigated Aya).

source.quote:
This step reduces harmful generations for adversarial
       prompts by 78–89% as judged by human experts.

findings.text: Professional-level jailbreak scenarios were explicitly out of scope for this study.

source.quote:
Professional-level jailbreak scenarios are out of
the scope for this study.

findings.text: Aya was not more prone to multilingual safety attacks than English; lower-capability languages sometimes produced less actionable harmful answers.

source.quote:
we find that the Aya model is not more prone to
safety attacks for languages other than English, as it has simply not been safety-mitigated for any

findings.text: Safety preamble at inference raised toxicity on open-ended prompts (~19% higher toxic outputs against racial/gender identity groups) despite helping refusals on harmful prompts.

source.quote:
as its probability of generating toxic outputs
against racial and gender identity groups increases by around 19%.

findings.text: Lower-resourced languages (Zulu, Gaelic) needed a higher safety-data mixture weight (3% vs 0.5%) for adequate [AdvBench](/evals/advbench) mitigation.

source.quote:
For Zulu and Gaelic, the two lowest-resource languages in our evaluation, a higher
distillation data weight (3%) is necessary for reducing the harmfulness sufficiently.

findings.text: Authors judge Aya Safe sufficiently safety-mitigated for adversarial-harm intents despite a small capability trade-off, while noting this covers only one aspect of large language model (LLM) safety.

source.quote:
we consider that Aya Safe is
sufficiently safety-mitigated with a small performance trade-off.

findings.text: Perspective API language bias may inflate German and Portuguese toxicity scores relative to other languages.

source.quote:
we caution the readers to keep the potential language bias
of Perspective API (the toxicity evaluator) in mind.

notes: Technical report (not a system card). Safety content is in §6–§7 and Appendix J/H/I. Skipped general capability suites (discriminative/generative held-outs, Dolly win rates, Flores/XLSum/TydiQA, XCOPA/XNLI, etc.). Skipped Jigsaw/CivilComments toxicity-classification AUC (Table 23) as classifier skill. Figures 11–12/14–17 are largely bar charts without reliable text-layer numbers; used Table 24, Tables 9–10, and prose averages for RTP. Aya Safe and Aya Beta are report variants without seed ids (rawModelName). Human AdvBench rates for unmitigated Aya given only as 89–90% range (finding, not evalResults). XSafety used for distillation training, not reported as a held-out score table. Preprint date Feb 13 2024 is not treated as model releaseDate.
